newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian firms to jointly build palm oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firms to jointly build palm oil refinery.

text.p: A consortium of four Malaysian firms entered into a memorandum of understanding on Friday to jointly build a 70 million ringgit palm oil refinery in eastern Sabah state.
Asiatic Development Bhd, Kuala Sidim Bhd, Palmco Holdings Bhd and Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd will each own a 25 percent stake in the joint venture.

The refinery, which is expected to commence operation in 1999, will have a processing capacity of between 800 and 1,000 tonnes per day. The consortium also plans to build a 300-tonne per day palm kernel crusher plant which is expected to begin operations a year later.
The companies said in a joint statement that the project would be financed through a combination of equity and bank borrowings.
The four groups have combined landholdings of 87,000 hectares in Sabah which would ensure consistent supplies of crude palm oil and palm kernel for the plants, the statement said.
